  <ui-highlight_box id="concept-evaporation" icon="☀️" title="1. Evaporation" text="The sun heats water in oceans, lakes and rivers. Liquid water turns into water vapor and rises into the atmosphere. Plants also release vapor through transpiration." accent="#f59e0b" style="outline" />

  <ui-highlight_box id="concept-condensation" icon="☁️" title="2. Condensation" text="As water vapor rises it cools and turns back into tiny liquid droplets around dust particles. Billions of droplets gather to form clouds." accent="#64748b" style="outline" />

  <ui-highlight_box id="concept-precipitation" icon="🌧️" title="3. Precipitation and Collection" text="When cloud droplets grow heavy enough, they fall as rain, snow, sleet or hail.   <ui-callout id="tip-callout" kind="tip" title="Remember" text="The water cycle has no start or end. The same water has been recycling for billions of years." />

In spring the snow melts, flows into a river, and returns to the ocean." code="Ocean -> evaporation -> vapor -> condensation -> cloud -> precipitation (snow) -> melt and runoff -> river -> Ocean" code_caption="One possible path of a single water drop." takeaway="Water changes state, but it is never used up." />
